text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
Robusta futures in London ended mixed in thin volume. September and November closed $15 higher at $1,630 per tonne. By contrast, January lost $11 to close at $1,580 per tonne.

Arabica futures in New York closed lower across the board. Traders said the move was a typical Monday pattern in the Brazilian winter, when cold weather fails to materialize and the outlook is for continued mild temperatures. The September/December switch narrowed to 24.60 cents/lb, down from 28 cents/lb on Friday. September lost 6.50 cents to close at 199.35 cents/lb, while December gave up 3.10 cents to close at 174.75 cents/lb.
UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 327 bags as of August 8 to 93,792 bags. There were 35 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

GUATEMALA - Coffee exports in 1997/98 (October/September) are forecast to reach 3.2 million 60-kg bags, significantly down on what will be shipped in 1996/97, when exports already reached 4.02 million bags as of August 7. A spokesman for the National Coffee Association (Anacafe) recently said that production in 1997/98 is likely to be a little bit lower than in the previous year without giving any precise numbers. The high level of exports in 1996/97 is difficult to explain given current production forecasts but Anacafe said contraband coffee from neighbouring countries was not the reason exports were higher than expected this year.

PANAMA ** - According to official sources, coffee production in 1996/97 (October/September) reached 215,000 60- kg bags, up from 205,000 bags produced the previous year. Production in 1997/98 is forecast at more than 220,000 bags.

IRELAND ** - Ireland imported 17,600 bags of coffee in January/February 1997 which compares to 9,600 bags the same two months in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 reached 114,400 bags, slightly less than the 114,900 bags imported the previous year. Ireland gets most of its coffee in the form of solubles from the UK.

SPAIN ** - Spain imported 373,005 bags of coffee in March 1997, 33 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 1.014 million bags, 16 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 12 per cent to 3.614 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/March 1997 were Uganda (267,000 vs 235,400 bags), Brazil (156,700 vs 74,600 bags) and Vietnam (139,200 vs 71,300 bags).

The country exported 169,700 bags of coffee in January/March 1997, 28 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose by nearly 50 per cent to 599,500 bags.PANAMBN
